title: Predicting electric-field noise in ion traps using fluctuation electrodynamics
authors: Markus Teller, Da An, Alberto M. Alonso, Philip C. Holz, Philipp Schindler, Hartmut Häffner, Tracy E. Northup
abstract: Electric-field noise in microfabricated surface ion traps contributes to gate errors in trapped-ion quantum computers, but this noise has been challenging to predict. Here, we present a method to predict the electric-field noise arising from fluctuations in the bulk of dielectric and metallic materials. The method is valid for arbitrary trap geometries, and the only relevant material property is energy loss. We apply it to an ion trap with an electrically floating electrode and find the contribution from dielectrics to be dominant. Our model predicts the observed noise for this trap within a factor of four. In addition, we apply our model to typical surface trap designs and analyze how the electrode structures shield the noise.
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive method to predict electric-field noise in surface ion traps by applying fluctuation electrodynamics to both dielectric and metallic components. Using FEA, the authors show that the noise is dominated by the substrate dielectrics and provide guidelines on how electrode geometry can be engineered to shield the trapped ion from these detrimental noise sources.
main_problem: The paper addresses the critical challenge of accurately predicting electric-field noise in microfabricated surface ion traps, as this noise directly causes gate errors in trapped-ion quantum computers.
main_result: The developed model successfully predicts the observed noise for a specific trap geometry within a factor of four, and it demonstrates that the noise is overwhelmingly dominated by dielectric fluctuations rather than metallic ones.
method: The authors employ a method rooted in the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, utilizing Finite-Element Analysis (FEA) to calculate the noise spectral density arising from fluctuating electric fields in both dielectric and metallic materials.
model_or_system: The system under study is a surface ion trap, where ions are trapped near metallic electrodes on a dielectric substrate. The model accounts for the geometry of the electrodes and the material properties (specifically energy loss) of the surrounding dielectrics and metals.
key_observables: Electric-field noise spectral density ($S_E$), motional heating rate ($\dot{ ar{n}}$), and trap frequencies ($\omega_z$).
important_parameters: Trap distance ($d$), electrode geometry parameters (trench width $a$, undercut width $b$, trench depth $c$), and the material loss tangent ($	an \delta$).
main_assumptions: The noise contributions from metals and dielectrics are assumed to be uncorrelated, and the analysis relies on solving Maxwell's equations using FEA.
figures_summary: Figures compare measured and simulated heating rates as a function of trap distance and electrode geometry parameters, showing how increasing trench depth or undercut width can mitigate noise.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the theoretical framework using the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, applies it using FEA to model noise from both dielectrics and metals, presents results on specific trap geometries, and concludes with systematic studies on how electrode structure modifies the noise profile.
why_interesting: This work provides a crucial, quantitative tool for designing next-generation quantum hardware. By linking fundamental material properties (loss tangent) to measurable quantum errors (heating rates), it guides the engineering of trap architectures to minimize decoherence.
